newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress set to elect new chief.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress set to elect new chief.

text.p: A Congress party stalwart emerged as a stopgap front-runner to replace former premier P.V. Narasimha Rao as head of India's oldest political party while the old guard and youth jostled for long-term leadership.
The 19-member Congress Working Committee was set to meet late on Monday to elect a provisional chief, members said.

Sitaram Kesri, veteran party treasurer, was tipped to be elected interim Congress chief to replace Rao, who stepped down on Saturday after a court upheld a summons ordering him to appear in a $100,000 criminal conspiracy case.
"Sitaram Kesri expected to take charge," the Economic Times said.
Kesri, the party's chief fund-raiser, was seen as a stopgap consensus candidate until the party's plenary body held internal elections later this year, party officials said.
"The struggle will be at the party's general session," V.N. Gadgil, a Congress general secretary, told Reuters.
The general session of the party, scheduled to be held in December, might be brought forward to resolve the long-term leadership issue, he said.
But the meeting was unlikely before elections in Uttar Pradesh, the most populous state, which end in early October.
"The party would not like to rock the boat before the Uttar Pradesh elections," B.G. Verghese, a analyst at the Centre for Policy Research, told Reuters.
Congress, in alliance with a low-caste party, has mounted a challenge to beat the powerful Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party in Uttar Pradesh.
Battered by a string of corruption charges against its leaders, Congress is searching for a clean face to guide it through the crisis.
"He (the new chief) should be a man with a clean character, impart confidence and guide the party to the future," Gadgil said.
Rao, 75, had been under pressure to step down after leading Congress to its worst defeat in general elections ended in May.
Congress has ruled India for all but four years since independence from British rule in 1947.
Seven ministers resigned from Rao cabinet early this year in a bribes-for-favour scandal. Former communications minister Sukh Ram was arrested last week in a corruption case.
"The party needs a dynamic man who can take up the challenge and keep the party united," Ved Prakash, a senior Congress leader, told Reuters.
A.K. Antony, a soft-spoken and upright Congress leader from the southern state of Kerala, was seen by many party leaders as a possible choice.
"Antony is a nice man and has the right image," a senior Congress leader said.
But Antony's lack of following among Congressmen in the northern states was seen as a handicap, analysts said.
Rao's former finance minister Manmohan Singh, who spearheaded the economic liberalisation drive in 1991, also has a clean public image but was seen largely as a technocrat.
The selection of a provisional chief would open the door to a fight among the many contenders for the longer-term leadership as they try to rally support.
